raw_text:
Below is a safe, progressive 12-week strength program tailored to a 30-year-old advanced lifter who is 20 weeks pregnant, cleared for moderate training. It respects pregnancy-specific guidelines: no supine work after week 16, no maximal attempts/valsava, avoid contact/impact, manage overheating and fatigue, emphasize pelvic floor and posture, and adjust as needed day-to-day. The aim is to maintain strength, movement quality, and comfort through the second trimester into the early third, with built-in autoregulation.

Global structure
- Frequency: 3 strength days/week + 1 optional accessories/mobility day
- Session length: 45–65 minutes
- Intensity: Moderate, leaving 2–4 reps in reserve (RIR). No grinding, no breath-holding; use controlled breathing.
- Main movements: Squat pattern, hinge, vertical/horizontal push and pull, unilateral lower body, carries, anti-rotation/core stability, pelvic floor work.
- Modifications for pregnancy:
  - Replace supine presses with incline/seated presses after week 16.
  - Wide stance or box for squats as bump grows; switch to goblet or safety bar if back squat uncomfortable.
  - Use trap bar/RDLs if conventional deadlift feels uncomfortable; avoid heavy mixed-grip strain.
  - Avoid lying prone; use incline or quadruped as needed.
  - Avoid ballistic/plyo; use controlled tempo.
  - Watch for coning/doming during core work; prioritize anti-extension/anti-rotation.
  - Stop any exercise that causes pain, dizziness, vaginal bleeding/fluid leakage, contractions, or unusual shortness of breath.
- Progression: Volume emphasis with stable load; small load nudges only if RPE allows. Shift to maintenance/stability by Weeks 9–12.
- Warm-up each session (8–12 min):
  - 3–5 min light cardio (bike, treadmill walk)
  - Dynamic mobility: cat-cow, open books, hip flexor rocks, adductor rocks, ankle pumps
  - Activation: banded face pulls 2x12, glute bridges (elevated torso) 2x12, bear breathing 2x5 breaths
- Breathing and bracing:
  - Exhale on exertion. Avoid prolonged valsalva. Consider 360 breathing and “zip up” pelvic floor gently on the effort.
- RPE/RIR:
  - Target RPE 6–7 (2–4 RIR) on compounds; RPE 5–6 on accessories.
- Rest intervals:
  - Compounds 90–150s, accessories 60–90s, core 45–60s.

Phases overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Groove patterns, moderate strength with submax sets, pelvic floor and posture emphasis.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Maintain strength, small volume uptick, unilateral control and anti-rotation.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Maintenance and comfort-first stability; reduce axial loading as needed, reinforce core/pelvic floor and upper back.

Weekly structure template
- Day A: Squat focus + horizontal push/pull + core
- Day B: Hinge focus + vertical push/pull + core
- Day C: Unilateral lower + mixed upper + carries + core
- Optional Day D: Accessories/mobility/conditioning (easy)

Exercise key/alternatives
- Squat: Back squat (high bar), safety bar squat, goblet squat to box.
- Hinge: Trap bar deadlift, RDL, kettlebell deadlift.
- Pressing: Incline DB press (30–45°), half-kneeling landmine press, seated DB press.
- Pulling: Chest-supported row, one-arm cable row, lat pulldown, assisted pull-up.
- Core: Pallof press/holds, dead bug variations (head/shoulders elevated if supine intolerant), bird-dog, quadruped T-spine rotations, side plank (elevated).
- Carries: Suitcase carry, farmer carry (light-moderate).
- Pelvic floor: Quick flicks and long holds, integrated with breath.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Establish strong, comfortable patterns; RPE ~6–7)
Week 1
- Day A
  - Safety bar squat or goblet squat to box: 4x6 @ RPE 6
  - Incline DB press (30–45°): 3x8 @ RPE 6
  - Chest-supported row: 3x10 @ RPE 6
  - Split squat (rear foot low): 3x8/side
  - Pallof press: 3x10/side, 2s hold
  - Pelvic floor: 6 quick flicks + 6x5s holds
- Day B
  - Trap bar deadlift (high handles if needed): 4x5 @ RPE 6–7
  - Half-kneeling landmine press: 3x8/side
  - Lat pulldown (neutral): 3x10
  - Hip hinge accessory: DB RDL: 3x8 @ RPE 6
  - Bird-dog: 3x6/side slow
  - Suitcase carry: 3x20–30m/side
- Day C
  - Front-foot-elevated split squat: 3x8/side
  - Seated cable row (neutral): 3x10
  - Incline push-up to rack: 3x8–10
  - 45° back extension (range as comfortable): 3x10
  - Side plank (elevated): 3x20–30s/side
  - Pelvic floor: 6 quick + 6x5s holds
- Optional Day D (easy)
  - 20–30 min brisk walk or bike + mobility flow 10 min

Week 2
- Keep exercises. If all sets ≤ RPE 6, add 2–5% load or 1 rep/set.
- Maintain all cues and breathing.
- Core swaps if doming appears: replace dead bug with side-lying heel slides.

Week 3
- Day A: Squat 5x5 @ RPE 6–7; Press 3x8–10; Row 3x10–12; Split squat 3x8; Pallof holds 3x20–30s.
- Day B: Trap bar 4x4–5; Landmine 4x6–8; Pulldown 3x8–10; DB RDL 3x8; Bird-dog 3x8/side; Suitcase carry 3x30–40m.
- Day C: FFE split squat 4x6–8; Seated row 3x10; Incline push-up 3x8–10; Back extension 3x10; Side plank 3x25–35s.

Week 4 (deload-light while practicing technique)
- Reduce volume ~25–30% or stop sets at RPE 6.
- Keep patterns, focus on tempo control (2–3s eccentric), longer rest.
- Maintain pelvic floor drills 3x/week.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Maintain strength; unilateral/anti-rotation emphasis)
Week 5
- Day A
  - Safety bar or goblet squat to box: 4x5 @ RPE 6–7
  - Incline DB press: 4x6–8
  - One-arm cable row: 4x8/side (anti-rotation stance)
  - Reverse lunge (from high box for control): 3x8/side
  - Pallof press to overhead: 3x8/side
  - Pelvic floor: 8 quick + 6x6–8s holds
- Day B
  - Trap bar deadlift: 4x4–5 @ RPE 6–7
  - Seated DB overhead press (neutral grip): 3x8
  - Wide-grip lat pulldown or assisted pull-up: 3x8–10
  - Hip thrust (shoulders elevated, head supported): 3x10 (ensure comfort; stop if pressure symptoms)
  - Bird-dog with row (band): 3x6/side
  - Suitcase carry: 4x20–30m/side
- Day C
  - Step-up (knee height moderate): 4x6–8/side
  - Cable chest press (standing split stance): 3x10
  - Chest-supported T‑raise/Y‑raise: 3x10–12
  - 45° back extension or hip hinge to wall: 3x10
  - Side plank on bench: 3x25–35s/side
  - Pelvic floor: 8 quick + 6x6–8s holds

Week 6
- Small load/rep progress if RIR≥3. If fatigue, hold steady.
- Swap in box squat width as bump grows; adjust range of motion as needed.

Week 7
- Day A: Squat 5x4–5; Incline press 4x6–8; 1-arm row 4x8; Reverse lunge 3x8; Pallof with step-out 3x8/side.
- Day B: Trap bar 4x4; Seated DB press 4x6–8; Pulldown 3x8–10; Hip thrust 3x8–10; Quadruped crawl (short sets) 4x10–15m if comfortable.
- Day C: Step-up 4x6–8; Cable chest press 3x10; Chest-supported rear delt 3x12; Hinge to wall 3x10; Side plank 3x30–40s.

Week 8 (deload-light)
- Cut 20–30% volume, maintain movement quality, prioritize recovery.
- Evaluate comfort with axial loading; prepare modifications for Phase 3.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Comfort-first maintenance; reduce axial loading if needed)
Goals: Maintain strength and posture with slightly lower intensity, emphasize upper back, hips, carries, and core stability. Keep sets crisp at RPE 5–6.

Week 9
- Day A
  - Goblet squat to box (or safety bar light): 4x6 @ RPE 5–6
  - Incline DB press: 3x8
  - Chest-supported row: 3x10
  - B-stance RDL (light): 3x8/side
  - Pallof iso-holds: 3x20–30s/side
  - Pelvic floor: 8 quick + 6x8–10s holds
- Day B
  - KB deadlift from blocks: 4x6
  - Half-kneeling landmine press: 3x8/side
  - Lat pulldown neutral: 3x10
  - Glute bridge (torso elevated) or hip thrust light: 3x10
  - Bird-dog slow: 3x6/side
  - Suitcase carry: 3–4x20–30m/side
- Day C
  - Step-up low box: 3x8/side
  - Cable chest press: 3x10
  - Seated row neutral: 3x10–12
  - Face pull: 3x12–15
  - Side plank elevated: 3x20–30s/side

Week 10
- Maintain or slightly progress reps if RIR≥3. Keep breathing strategy strict.
- Substitute machines if free weights feel unstable (leg press with limited depth, seated row, machine chest press incline).

Week 11
- Day A: Goblet to box 4x6; Incline DB 3x8–10; Chest-supported row 3x10–12; B-stance RDL 3x8; Pallof 3x10/side.
- Day B: KB deadlift blocks 4x5–6; Landmine press 3x8; Pulldown 3x10; Glute bridge 3x10–12; Bird-dog 3x8/side; Farmer carry light 3x20m.
- Day C: Step-up 3x8; Cable chest press 3x10; Seated row 3x12; Face pull 3x12–15; Side plank 3x25–35s.

Week 12 (taper for comfort/readiness)
- Reduce volume 25–40%. Keep movement, reduce load if any discomfort.
- Add more mobility and breathwork. End sessions with 5–8 minutes easy walk.

Core and pelvic floor guidelines
- Frequency: 3–4x/week integrated as above.
- Focus on:
  - 360 breathing: inhale to ribs/back, gentle pelvic floor relaxation; on exertion exhale and gently “lift and zip” pelvic floor at 20–30% effort.
  - Avoid crunches/sit-ups, aggressive planks if coning appears.
  - Anti-rotation/anti-extension: Pallof, bird-dog, dead bug with head/shoulders elevated or side-lying variations.
- Red flags to stop and modify: coning/doming, urinary leakage, pelvic heaviness/pressure, pubic symphysis pain.

Autoregulation and substitutions
- On any day with higher fatigue, nausea, pelvic or low back discomfort:
  - Swap back squat → goblet squat to box; trap bar → KB block pull; split squats → step-ups; overhead press → landmine/seated DB; rowing → chest-supported/seated cable.
  - Keep RPE ≤6 and cut 1 set per exercise.
- Symphysis or SI discomfort:
  - Narrow split stance, reduce depth, use bands for hip stability, avoid single-leg if painful, favor bilateral limited range patterns.

Conditioning/mobility (2–3x/week, 15–25 min)
- Low-impact: incline treadmill walk, bike, elliptical, pool walking.
- Keep conversational pace; avoid overheating; hydrate.

Recovery and lifestyle guidelines
- Warm environment management: train in cool, ventilated space; avoid hot studios or saunas.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.0 L/day, plus 500–700 ml per hour of training; include electrolytes if cramping or heavy sweater.
- Nutrition (general, coordinate with OB/dietitian):
  - Energy: modest surplus as advised for second trimester if needed; prioritize satiety and energy.
  - Protein: ~1.6–2.0 g/kg/day from varied sources.
  - Carbs: fuel training, especially pre/post; include fiber and fruits/veg.
  - Fats: include healthy fats; DHA per OB guidance.
  - Pre-training snack 60–90 min prior (e.g., yogurt + fruit); post-training protein 20–30 g.
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; left-side lying preferred; use pillows for hip/abdomen support.
- Footwear: supportive; consider belly band if comfort improves lifting tolerance.

Monitoring
- Use RPE log and symptom log each session (breathlessness rating, pelvic floor symptoms, back/pubic pain, dizziness).
- If any warning signs occur (bleeding, fluid leak, regular painful contractions, chest pain, severe headache, visual changes, decreased fetal movement, calf pain/swelling), stop and follow medical guidance.

This plan keeps her strong, maintains muscle, and supports posture and pelvic health through weeks 20–32 of pregnancy, with flexible, safe modifications as needed.
